cards.title: Constraints Breed Innovation
cards.insight: The most creative breakthroughs often emerge when resources are limited or rules are imposed. Limitations force us to think laterally, abandon conventional approaches, and discover novel solutions we might never have explored with unlimited freedom.
cards.takeaway: This week, identify one constraint in a project you're working on and deliberately use it as a creative prompt rather than an obstacle.

cards.title: Cross-Domain Collision
cards.insight: Creativity accelerates when ideas from unrelated fields intersect. A painter studying particle physics, a musician learning architecture, or an engineer reading poetry creates novel neural pathways that spawn unexpected innovations.
cards.takeaway: Spend 20 minutes exploring a domain completely outside your expertise and ask: 'What would this look like if I applied this principle to my work?'

cards.title: Permission from Failure
cards.insight: Creative people reframe failure as permission to experiment more boldly next time. Each failed attempt removes one wrong path, clarifies what doesn't work, and builds confidence to attempt increasingly ambitious ideas.
cards.takeaway: Document one recent failure and extract two specific insights about what to try differently—treat it as creative research rather than defeat.

cards.title: Boredom as Fertile Ground
cards.insight: Minds at rest generate more creative associations than minds under constant stimulation. Boredom, discomfort, and idle time activate the default mode network, where the brain makes unexpected connections and generates novel ideas.
cards.takeaway: Protect at least 15 minutes today for unfocused time—no phone, no task—and observe what your mind naturally wanders toward.
